title: All the new movies and TV shows streaming now (August 2026)
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: "Ted Lasso" Season 4 premieres on Apple TV on August 5, 2026, with Jason Sudeikis leading AFC Richmond's women's team.
"Reacher" Season 4 starring Alan Ritchson streams on Prime Video starting August 14, 2026, continuing the vigilante justice series.
Netflix presents "The Whisper Man" on August 29, 2026, featuring Robert De Niro, Michelle Monaghan, and Adam Scott in the new film.

title: A longtime 7News reporter is signing off
author: John Waller
bullets: Kimberly Bookman is leaving 7News Boston after 12 years, with her last broadcast set for Tuesday.
Bookman joined 7News in 2014, previously working in Manchester, Baltimore, Spartanburg, and Elmira.
She plans to remain in the Boston area but has not disclosed her next professional move.

title: Cambridge man dies after being pulled from waters off Martha’s Vineyard
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: 55-year-old Kevin Foster from Cambridge died after a swimming incident at Long Point Wildlife Refuge, Martha's Vineyard.
First responders, including lifeguards, rescued multiple distressed swimmers; Foster was taken to Martha's Vineyard Hospital.
State Rep. Marjorie Decker helped launch a GoFundMe for Foster's family, raising over $74,000.

title: Drake Maye runs through scouting report of Patriots’ crowded receiver room
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye highlights the value of each of the Patriots' seven wide receivers during training camp discussions.
Maye praises A.J. Brown for his route craft and leadership in the Patriots' receiver group.
Kayshon Boutte is noted for his reliability and consistent playmaking abilities, according to Maye.

title: Why one MLB analyst labeled Red Sox trade for Adley Rutschman as a ‘wild overpay on the face of it’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: The Red Sox acquired catcher Adley Rutschman from the Orioles, trading Carlos Narváez and prospects for him.
ESPN analyst Kiley McDaniel criticized the trade as a 'wild overpay', noting concerns about the high price paid.
McDaniel believes traded prospects Eyanson, Witherspoon, and Azocar could become legitimate MLB players.

title: David Sedaris on Duolingo, death, and dressing like a priest
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: David Sedaris's new essay collection, 'The Land and Its People,' addresses his addiction to Duolingo games.
The book explores Sedaris's feelings on family relationships and his father's death at age 98.
Sedaris revealed his secret marriage to longtime partner Hugh Hamrick in his latest book.

title: John C. Reilly jumped on stage to sing at a Boston dive bar
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: John C. Reilly performed impromptu at Tavern at the End of the World in Charlestown, singing with local band Bosstown Heavy.
Reilly joined in for songs, including '54-46 (That’s My Number)' by Toots and the Maytals, at the Boston dive bar.
The actor was in the area for at least 10 days, participating in the Newport Folk Festival and performing locally.

title: Mass. woman found after going missing for 27 hours in N.H. woods
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Megan Kelley, 39, from Fall River, went missing from Dolly Copp Campground in New Hampshire on Saturday.
A couple hiking in Gorham found Kelley 27 hours later lying on the side of an access road.
Kelley was taken to Androscoggin Valley Hospital in Berlin; she suffered no life-threatening injuries.

title: Plymouth woman dies after tree falls on her porch
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: A 61-year-old Plymouth woman died after a tree fell on her porch on Sullivan Avenue, authorities reported.
Emergency responders found her trapped under the tree; she later died from her injuries at a local hospital.
Strong winds and heavy rain, with over 2 inches in Plymouth, likely caused the tree to collapse.

title: There’s a pig loose on Martha’s Vineyard, apparently
author: Peter Chianca
bullets: A pig is loose on Martha's Vineyard, prompting an all-points bulletin from Edgartown Police.
The wandering pig was last seen on Chase Road, heading toward Dark Woods Road on Sunday morning.
Residents are advised to contact Edgartown Animal Control instead of attempting to corral the pig themselves.
